data.long_meaning: The name May is derived from the Greek word Maia, meaning ‘mother’. This name was also used for the Roman goddess of fertility, Matrona. In Christian tradition, May is associated with the Virgin Mary and the month of May, a time of growth and renewal. The name May carries the meaning “Mythos: Goddess of fertility, Matrona: Mother goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose May usually hope their child will grow to embody mythos: goddess of fertility, matrona: mother goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Μάη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μάη προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'μάη', που σημαίνει 'μητέρα' ή 'η μεγάλη'. Στην αρχαία Ελλάδα, το όνομα συνδέθηκε με τη θεά Μάη, μητέρα των θεών. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα μπορεί να συμβολίζει τη μητρική αγάπη και προστασία.

in_latin.name: Maia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Maiae originem habet in lingua Latina, ubi 'maia' significat 'terra' vel 'mater'. In traditione Christiana, nomen Maiae potest referri ad naturam, vitam, et maternitatem. Ea quae fertilitatem et abundantiam repraesentat.

In many cultures around the world, May is also known as a month of celebration, with a number of holidays and festivals taking place during this time.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name May is often linked to the Virgin Mary, who is celebrated as the mother of Jesus, the son of God. For those who hold the name May, it can be seen as a reminder to nurture and care for others, and to seek spiritual growth and renewal in their own lives.
